Cells are the basic structural and functional units of life. An animal cell has a cell membrane that controls movement of substances into and out of the cell.
The nucleus contains genetic information stored in DNA. DNA provides instructions used to make proteins.
Ribosomes assemble proteins by translating messenger RNA. Ribosomes may be free in the cytoplasm or attached to rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Mitochondria produce much of the cell's ATP through cellular respiration. ATP is used to power many cellular processes.
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins and lipids for delivery. Lysosomes break down materials using enzymes.
These organelles work together. The nucleus stores instructions, ribosomes build proteins, mitochondria supply energy, and the Golgi apparatus packages products.
